definition: Universally perfect means lacking none of the perfections found in things (ST I q.4 a.2). These preexist in God eminently, not as a conjunction of incompatible creaturely forms. IsPerfect InAct g := ∀ x r, InAct x r → InAct g r uses InAct in its formal-or-virtual sense (DEF-IN-ACT-FORMALLY, DEF-IN-ACT-VIRTUALLY).
note: The source sense constrains how perfection-respects and InAct are read. Lean's arbitrary Respect and InAct parameters do not independently enforce the formal-or-eminent interpretation. DISAMB-IN-ACT records the unresolved formal/virtual choice: a result must interpret its one InAct parameter consistently in every premise, and defend those premises under that choice. This definition does not automatically combine the senses or settle that premise-truth obligation.
